newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Sabena, Swissair and Austrian chose Airbus.
newsitem.headline: Sabena, Swissair and Austrian chose Airbus.

text.p: The Swiss airline Swissair and its partners Austrian Airlines and Belgium's Sabena have chosen Airbus A330-200 aircraft to renew their long-distance fleet, Sabena said on Thursday.
Boeing's B767 aircraft lost out in the battle for the initial order for 14 of the 256-passenger aircraft with options on up to 15 more, a Sabena spokesman said. He declined to give financial details.
The three European airlines also said they were planning to launch joint operations across the Atlantic with Delta Air Lines from next February.

Sabena said the first of the twin-engined A330-200s -- a smaller version of the A330 -- will be assembled in Toulouse, France with the maiden flight scheduled for August 1997. The three airlines will receive the first of the aircraft in September 1998, it said.

Swissair, which has a 49.5 percent stake in Sabena and 10 percent in Austrian, will replace eight Airbus A310-300s with nine A330-200s at a net cost of 300 to 400 million Swiss francs ($225 million to $300 million). Four will be bought outright and five leased, while the company has an option on a further 10.

Austrian said it had placed a firm order for four A330-200s worth some four billion schillings ($365 million). It said the first plane was expected to be delivered in August 1998 and the second one at the beginning of 1999.
Sabena will immediately order one A330-200 and take an option on up to five more A330-200s, due to be delivered by 2000.
Swissair said it also planned to acquire three additional McDonnell Douglas MD11s before 1998 and would make a decision on replacing its five Boeing 747s later.
Sabena said the decision was approved earlier this week by the boards of directors of the three airlines, which have also linked their frequent flyer programmes.

"The partnership...has allowed a grouped order," the Sabena statement said. "Austrian Airlines, Sabena and Swissair work together within the framework of the purchase and management of these new planes."
Sabena said it would sell its three A310 planes in early 1997 to the U.S. plane leasing company ILFC. It will lease three A330-300s until the delivery of the ordered A330-200.
From 1997 its long-distance fleet will consist of four A340s, three A330s and two Boeing 747s. But the airline said it planned to concentrate on just one type of aircraft by 2000.
Sabena said the partners chose the Airbus A330 because it had an identical configuration with that of the A340 and offered synergies between the three partners.
Sabena said that harmonising its fleet would substantially reduce costs through savings in personnel training and technical support.
"Thanks to this decision...Sabena is hoping to save a few hundreds of millions (of Belgian francs)," it said.
